security.note: All 4 ACLs target res.partner.grade: read for base.group_user; full CRUD for base.group_system and sales_team.group_sale_manager; create/read/write (no unlink) for sales_team.group_sale_salesman. Grades are managed under CRM > Configuration.

views.note: res.partner.grade form/list/search + a stat button (partners_count/partners_label) drilling to grade members; inline view extensions add grade_id to res.partner, grade_id + 'partnership' tracking to product.template, partners_count to product.pricelist, and partnership_label to res.config.settings. The CRM config menu 'crm_menu_partners' is labelled from company.partnership_label.

behavioral_notes.element: sale.order.action_confirm -> _add_partnership (cross-model side-effect: order confirmation grades the customer)
behavioral_notes.observation: action_confirm() calls super() then _add_partnership(). _add_partnership iterates the orders and, for each whose assigned_grade_id is set, writes so.partner_id.commercial_partner_id.grade_id = so.assigned_grade_id — i.e. confirming a sale that contains a 'Membership / Partnership' product promotes the buying customer's COMMERCIAL (top-level company) partner to that grade. Metadata shows only the assigned_grade_id Many2one; it cannot show that confirmation mutates res.partner on a different record (commercial_partner_id, not necessarily the order's contact). assigned_grade_id itself is computed by _compute_partnership (@api.depends('order_line.product_id')): it filters order_line where service_tracking == 'partnership' and takes the first product_id.grade_id, so a non-partnership order yields an empty grade and _add_partnership is a no-op.

behavioral_notes.element: res.partner.write (grade assignment forces the grade's default pricelist onto the partner)
behavioral_notes.observation: res.partner overrides write(vals): when vals sets grade_id and that grade has a default_pricelist_id, it injects vals['specific_property_product_pricelist'] = grade.default_pricelist_id.id BEFORE super().write — so grading a partner (whether by the sale.order confirm flow above or a manual edit) silently also re-points the partner's specific pricelist to the level's pricelist. If the same write also tries to set a different specific_property_product_pricelist / property_product_pricelist, it raises UserError('You are trying to assign two different pricelists (one directly and one from grade (%(grade_name)s)).'). Net chain proven by tests/test_partnership.test_sell_basic_partnership: confirm -> partner.grade_id == product.grade_id AND partner.specific_property_product_pricelist == grade.default_pricelist_id. This propagation is pure Python and invisible in field metadata.

A constraint blocks any sale.order whose order lines reference products carrying more than one distinct product_id.grade_id (len(set(...)) > 1) with ValidationError('You cannot confirm Sale Order %(sale_order_name)s because there are products assigning different grades.'). This guarantees a single, unambiguous grade can be derived per order before _add_partnership runs — a business rule enforced in code, not expressible as a field/constraint in metadata. Confirmed by tests/test_partnership.test_constrains_uniqueness_partnership_grade.

product.template adds the Selection value ('partnership','Membership / Partnership') to service_tracking (ondelete set default) and grade_id ('Assigned Level'); it overrides _get_saleable_tracking_types() to append 'partnership' so membership/partnership service products pass the saleable-product domain (verified by test_partnership_product_domain). sale.order.line.service_tracking is a related on product_id.service_tracking, which is how _compute_partnership detects partnership lines. Reporting fields are computed via grouped reads metadata can't express: res.partner.grade._compute_partners_count and product.pricelist._compute_partners_count both _read_group res.partner (by grade_id, and by specific_property_product_pricelist respectively) to count affiliated partners; res.config.settings._onchange_partnership_label live-renames the ir.ui.menu 'partnership.crm_menu_partners' to the new label.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, no asset bundles (gap #3). The module is backend/ORM only: UI is plain XML views (res.partner.grade form/list/search, a stat button, and inline grade_id/pricelist field additions). No client-side widget or service.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: partnership owns one transactional-adjacent master model (res.partner.grade, the partner level) and otherwise extends the Sales document chain: product.template (a 'Membership / Partnership' service product), sale.order, res.partner and product.pricelist. Its defining behavior is a value-chain primary-activity side-effect, not shared IT plumbing: confirming a sale.order that contains a partnership product (sale.order.action_confirm -> _add_partnership) promotes the buying customer's commercial partner to the product's grade_id, and grading the partner (res.partner.write) grants the grade's default_pricelist_id. So the module rides the Quote-to-Cash flow (Stabell & Fjeldstad 'chain' — sequential value creation through the order document; Porter primary 'Marketing & Sales') to monetise membership and then tier customers. APQC 3.0 'Market and Sell Products and Services' fits because the trigger is selling a membership/partnership product through the order pipeline (depends crm+sale; the grade UI hangs under the CRM Configuration menu, and grade ACLs are keyed to the sales_team salesperson/manager groups). It is NOT 'support'/13.0 master-data management: although the end artefact (partner grade + pricelist) is partner master data, partnership does not merely maintain that data as firm infrastructure — it generates it as the outcome of a confirmed sale, i.e. a sales transaction effect. 9.0 (Manage Customer Service) and 11.0/13.0 were rejected: there is no service-request, finance or pure data-governance object here; the substance is sell-the-membership-then-grade-and-price-the-customer, which is squarely Market & Sell.

standard_capabilities: Partner levels/grades (res.partner.grade) with sequence, per-company scope and an optional default pricelist
Membership/partnership service product (service_tracking='partnership') carrying the grade it confers
Automatic grade assignment to the commercial partner on sale-order confirmation
Automatic grade-based pricelist application on the partner (with conflict guard)
Members-per-grade / members-per-pricelist counters with drill-through stat button
Configurable affiliate label (Members/Partners/Alumni) relabelling the CRM menu
typical_fits: Selling a yearly membership/partnership SKU and having the buyer auto-promoted to Gold/Silver/Bronze
Granting tiered pricelists to members purely by selling them the right membership product
Renaming the affiliate concept per organisation (association 'Members' vs reseller 'Partners')
common_gaps: No grade expiry / renewal / downgrade logic — the grade and pricelist persist until manually changed (no time-bound membership lifecycle)
Grade is applied only on action_confirm; cancelling/refunding the order does not revoke the grade or pricelist
assigned_grade_id is computed and non-stored, so there is no historical record of which order conferred a grade beyond res.partner grade_id tracking
No partner-facing portal/website membership purchase flow (backend sale.order only; frontend gap #3 is empty)
One grade per order and first-match selection — multi-tier or stacked memberships need customisation

open_questions: There is no revocation path: should cancelling/refunding a membership sale.order remove the grade and pricelist, or is the grade intended to be permanent until manually changed?
Membership lifecycle (expiry, renewal, downgrade between Gold/Silver/Bronze) is not modelled — is it expected to be handled by a complementary module or subscription product?

default_pricelist_id is optional on a grade; the intended behaviour when a graded partner already has a manually-set specific pricelist is to raise UserError on simultaneous conflict, but ordering/precedence of pre-existing pricelists vs. a later grade change is config-dependent.
